jobs.title: Staff Backend Graph Engineer
jobs.description: Why Socure ? Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day. We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading. About the Job Build the graph that decides who’s real. Every day, Socure’s Identity Graph helps businesses decide whether to trust the person on the other side of a screen. It links billions of signals (names, addresses, devices, emails, phones) into one picture of identity, and it does this in milliseconds. Fraudsters move fast. The graph has to be faster. As a Staff Engineer on this team, you’ll set the technical direction for the platform behind that decision. You’ll own hard problems end to end, work across Engineering, Data Science, Product, and Security, and see your work shape the products that protect millions of people. What You Will Do Shape the graph. Define the schemas, relationships, and ontology that make identity data consistent and extensible. Own entity resolution at scale. Decide how records, people, devices, and addresses connect, and how confident we are, across data that is messy, sparse, and sometimes adversarial. Build for speed and volume. Design batch and real-time pipelines, low-latency APIs, and serving systems that hold up under heavy load. Power fraud intelligence. Ship the production systems behind our ML features, model inference, and graph analytics. Move the numbers. Improve performance, reliability, and cost, and prove it with measurements. Set the direction. Lead architecture decisions, document the tradeoffs, and carry initiatives from first design through production rollout. Raise the bar. Mentor engineers and set the standard for design reviews, testing, CI/CD, and operations. Protect identity data. Build privacy, security, and PII protection into every system from day one. Your toolkit: Java, Scala, or Python. Spark, Kafka, Flink, Airflow, and AWS, including EMR. Graph technologies like Neo4j and Amazon Neptune. What You Will Bring Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or related field 7+ years building and running distributed systems in the cloud, with at least 2 at Staff or Senior Staff scope, or the equivalent Production scale you can quantify. You can tell us what you built, how big it was, and how much you improved latency, reliability, or cost Deep Spark, Kafka, or Flink experience in both batch and streaming, including debugging them in production Low-latency serving. You have built and tuned APIs where milliseconds matter Graph or entity-resolution experience. You have modeled connected data, matched records across noisy sources, or built an identity graph. Fraud or identity verification is a strong plus Cloud and operations fluency. AWS, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and real production observability ML data pipelines on Databricks, SageMaker, or similar, plus orchestration with Airflow or equivalent Technical leadership. You have led ambiguous, cross-team work, mentored engineers, and changed the direction of a system through design docs and influence, not authority What This Job is Not It’s not a role for someone who hasn’t owned a system end to end in production, including being on call for it. It’s not feature work on platforms someone else designed. It’s not a defined backlog. You’ll frame ambiguous problems yourself. It’s not a place to treat data privacy as a compliance checkbox. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. If you need an accommodation during any stage of the application or hiring process—including interview or onboarding support—please reach out to your Socure recruiting partner directly. Follow Us! ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. How we work High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. Working knowledge of AI and Inference, cloud infrastructure, and how modern software gets deployed and operated, with awareness of the Kubernetes ecosystem. jobs.description: 1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that. But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens. We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better. About engineering at Headway: Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!). We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they’re facing. This is a senior IC role — the person who owns the architecture of how Headway communicates at scale. You’ll design and evolve the decision engine, experimentation layer, and channel orchestration that will define how Headway reaches patients and providers for years to come. You’ll set the technical direction for a multi-vendor communications stack, own the unified message ledger, and bring LLM-powered personalization from concept to production. This role is high-leverage and cross-functional. You’ll work closely with marketing, CX, product, and the patient org — and your work will directly impact patient acquisition, retention, and health outcomes. A systems thinker who holds the architecture of a complex, multi-vendor platform and guides the team through it An engineer who has shipped high-throughput, event-driven systems in production and knows what reliability requires A communicator who translates technical trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders and drives alignment across marketing, product, and engineering Genuinely excited about the intersection of AI and communications — and thoughtful about what makes AI-in-the-loop systems reliable at scale A leader who earns influence through technical depth and leaves teams more capable than they found them Experience we’re seeking 8+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful time at Staff-level or equivalent Designed and built high-volume, event-driven communications platforms — email, SMS, push, or equivalent — at millions of events per month Fluency with multi-vendor delivery stacks; strong opinions about build-vs-buy trade-offs at the platform layer Experience building or working closely with experimentation infrastructure — A/B testing, engagement analytics, personalization, or recommendation systems Exposure to LLM-powered systems in production — not just API consumption, but thinking about reliability, latency, and quality at scale Demonstrated ability to shape technical direction across teams without direct authority Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave. The role We build internal systems to the same standard as our public products: specified, tested, reviewed and observable. We want engineers who enjoy that rigour and take full ownership of what they ship. What you will do Design and deliver systems and platforms, including intuitive UIs Build Go services and APIs that connect many data sources Design data models and architecture for connected systems Turn data into clear dashboards and visualisations Build LLM-powered features into everyday workflows Write specs, estimate work and deliver to agreed criteria Set a high bar in code review, testing and documentation Partner with non-technical colleagues to turn needs into tools Mentor engineers and improve how the team works Who you are You have deep expertise in at least two of: Back-end services in Go Modern front-end engineering [React/Svelte/TypeScript] Data engineering and analytics Data visualisation Applied LLM/ML in production workflows You also: Treat testing, security, performance and accessibility as part of the job Handle sensitive people data with care Write clearly and work well in a distributed team Own your work from first spec to production Nice to have : Python, Go, React, Svelte, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, a history of building tools for HR, finance or operations. This team will help us gain insights into the business and our talent pool, and use those insights to improve the experience of working at Canonical. As a Workplace Engineer at Canonical, you need an analytical, data-driven mind and a passion to connect and make sense of interesting data from APIs. We focus heavily on the collection of metrics, optimising processes, and ways of working across Canonical. You need to demonstrate leadership, excellence, and consistency and will mentor others in the team. What we offer colleagues We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description: Upbound is redefining how modern infrastructure is built for the Agentic AI Era. We’re the creators and primary maintainers of Crossplane , and we’re building the Intelligent Control Plane —a new platform layer that makes infrastructure programmable, autonomous, and composable . Our mission is to power the AI-native enterprise with a foundational platform layer that helps teams provision, operate, and adapt infrastructure at scale—so platforms are ready for both humans and AI agents . We partner with leading cloud providers, ISVs, and open-source communities to help organizations move faster with greater confidence. Today, Upbound supports Fortune 500 companies and platform engineers across 100+ countries . Crossplane has surpassed 100M+ downloads and is used by 1,000+ teams worldwide . We’re a Series B company backed by GV (formerly Google Ventures), Altimeter Capital, and Intel Capital , and we’ve raised $69M to date. Learn more at upbound.io Upbound is hiring a Senior Software Engineer to help us build and operate Upbound Spaces, the multiple control plane management software at the heart of the Upbound Platform. As part of the Spaces team, you will help us scale Upbound to reliably support thousands of control planes, while also extending enterprise control plane management and operations both in the cloud and on premises. Our team is expanding, and this is the perfect opportunity for you to make a significant engineering impact in both development and production operations. What You'll Do Actively build and operate Upbound Spaces in production, troubleshooting and resolving issues across multi-tenant SaaS environments, as well as contributing to Upbound's open-source projects, including Crossplane. Take ownership of building features in high demand by Upbound's customers and deliver new functionality that will delight and amaze our users. Investigate and debug complex issues in customer environments, including multi-control plane scenarios, resource reconciliation problems, and performance bottlenecks. Communicate through thoughtful and thorough design documents for new initiatives and detailed post-incident reviews that drive system improvements. Support the full project lifecycle for highly scalable and reliable services running in a cloud environment – discovery, analysis, architecture, design, review, documentation, building, migration, automation, deployment, production-readiness, and ongoing operational support. Write and maintain Go code that interfaces with the Kubernetes API, such as operators, controllers, add-ons, etc., with a focus on observability, debuggability, and operational excellence. Deploy, manage, and troubleshoot our Kubernetes services in production, using metrics, logs, and traces to identify and resolve issues quickly. Build and maintain operational tooling for debugging customer environments, analyzing control plane health, and automating incident response. Author documentation, user guides, runbooks, and blog posts to support and promote new features that you release. Support the software release cycle for Spaces self-hosted distributions, including diagnosing issues in customer-managed deployments. Participate in on-call rotation to support Upbound Cloud, responding to incidents and driving them to resolution. What You'll Bring Have experience operating production cloud services at scale: monitoring, alerting, incident response, post-mortems, and continuous improvement of service reliability. Have strong debugging skills across distributed systems, including experience with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing) and techniques for diagnosing issues in production environments. Have experience building and operating controllers that interact with the Kubernetes API server, including troubleshooting reconciliation loops, managing API rate limits, and optimizing controller performance. Are comfortable working directly with customers to understand, reproduce, and resolve complex technical issues in their environments. Take responsibility and ownership for solving problems even if they are outside your lane, especially during incidents affecting customer workloads. Demonstrate excellence in your work, constantly trying to improve your skills and the operational posture of the systems you build. Have empathy for customers and keep them in mind as you build solutions, understanding that reliability and debuggability are features. Realize the importance of clear communication and effective collaboration to work as a team, deliver great results, and support customers through technical challenges. Help create a safe environment where everyone can contribute, learn from failures, share on-call knowledge, and help each other grow as operators and engineers. #LI-REMOTE Why Upbound? At Upbound, you’ll help shape the systems and strategies that drive predictable, scalable growth in a product-led company embracing usage-based models. If you're excited to build from the ground up, work with cutting-edge cloud technologies, and directly impact how revenue is generated and scaled—this is your seat at the table. About Upbound Upbound is pioneering infrastructure platforms for the Agentic AI Era, serving Fortune 500 companies and platform engineers across more than 100 countries. The company empowers infrastructure and platform teams with Intelligent Control Planes - based on Kubernetes and Crossplane - that provision, operate, and adapt so platforms are ready for both humans and AI agents. Upbound is the creator and primary maintainer of Crossplane, the popular open-source framework for building cloud-native control planes, with over 100 million downloads and adoption by more than 1,000 teams worldwide. A Series B startup backed by GV (formerly Google Ventures), Altimeter Capital, and Intel Capital, Upbound has raised $69M to date. For more information, visit www.upbound.io .

jobs.description:
Principal Engineer

Location: Waterloo, London, England, UK | Hybrid (1 day per week in office)

Who We Are 

At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions consultancy that partners with organisations from early-stage startups to the world s largest companies. We take on hard software challenges and turn them into durable results. We build agentic products, the platforms they run on, and the engineering and design at every layer.

Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.

If this kind of work and our kind of people energises you, you’ve found the right place. 

Who You Are

And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us! We invest heavily in digital-first operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time. You'll sequence the work so every stage ships usable improvements each month, and design the process so it can be run by AI agents as well as by people. Interest in performance engineering and low-latency systems. The software in the middle has to be right every time. A message processed twice, a lost update, or a record shown to the wrong tenant is a compliance failure for our customers. You’ll work on the core platform that carries this data between institutions around the world, written in Go. As a Staff Engineer on the team you’ll build the hardest parts of it, contribute to its design, and help the engineers around you do their best work. What You'll Do Design and build core parts of our transaction platform. Build for correctness under failure, with the isolation and auditability a regulated product needs. Scale the platform as transaction volume and the number of institutions per node grow, keeping latency predictable and the database healthy. Write design docs for what you build, and give sharp, useful reviews on other people’s designs and code. Build with AI agents every day, and help improve the specs, context and review practices that make agent-written code safe to ship in a regulated product. Work with product, compliance and customer-facing teams to turn regulatory and customer needs into working software. Own what you ship in production, from tracing and alerts to incident follow-ups. Mentor engineers on the team. Work on an on call rotation Must Haves Systems design depth. You’ve designed and owned distributed systems where correctness matters more than features. Typically 8+ years building backend systems. Clear, concise writing in a remote company that makes decisions in documents and async threads. Security fundamentals for sensitive data: encryption in transit and at rest, key handling, minimising personal data, and least-privilege access. jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer, Digital Employee Experience

San Francisco, California

GAQ427R232

At Databricks, we are on a mission to help data teams solve the world s toughest problems. The Digital Employee Experience team builds the internal tools, platforms, and data systems that power how every Brickser works. From procurement applications and SaaS inventory systems to mobile apps, AI-powered tools, and data pipelines that serve IT.

As a Senior Software Engineer on this team, you will own projects end-to-end and be the team lead of software engineers. You will own architecture, design, implementation, deployment, and stakeholder management. You ll build production web and mobile applications on the Databricks Platform, design data pipelines that ingest from dozens of SaaS systems, and ship AI-powered integrations (MCP servers, LLM features) that reduce friction across the entire company. This is a high-autonomy, high-impact role where you operate with a startup mentality inside a scaled organization.

The impact you will have

  • Design, build, and maintain production full-stack applications (web and mobile) used company-wide. Such as, but not limited to, procurement platforms, employee experience apps, SaaS management tools, and mobile apps for leadership.
  • Build and own data pipelines that ingest, transform, and serve data from SaaS systems into Databricks, ensuring data quality and pipeline reliability.
  • Architect and implement authentication and authorization flows using Okta, OAuth, and service principals.
  • Build and deploy MCPs  that connect internal tools to AI assistants, and contribute to AI-powered features, including LLM-based classification, data enrichment, and prompt-based guardrails.
  • Design and manage CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, and deployment automation using GitHub, HashiCorp Vault, and Databricks tooling.
  • Improve and enforce SWE  standards for the team: PR review processes, testing frameworks, and environment management (dev/staging/prod).
  • Work directly with stakeholders across Security, Legal, HR, Finance, and Engineering to gather requirements, navigate trade-offs, and deliver solutions.
  • Author design documents, PRDs, and architecture proposals for new systems and features.
  • Mentor contractors and junior engineers. Delegate work, break down roadmap items, and drive project planning with minimal management oversight.
  • Drive roadmap planning for your domain by identifying high-impact work and autonomously sequencing it.

What we look for

  • Bachelor s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of production software development experience, with demonstrated full-stack proficiency (backend, frontend, and data).
  • Strong experience with Python as a primary language, with production experience building full-stack applications.
  • Experience designing and deploying applications on cloud platforms (AWS and/or Azure).
  • Hands-on experience with data engineering — building ETL/ELT pipelines, working with structured and semi-structured data.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD, IaC, and modern DevOps practices (GitHub Actions, Terraform, Docker).
  • Experience with SaaS platforms or service-oriented architectures.
  • Experience with security and systems that handle sensitive data: identity management, access control, RBAC/RLS patterns.
  • Strong communication skills. You  can write a clear design doc, present to cross-functional stakeholders, and navigate technical trade-offs with non-technical audiences.
  • Experience with AI/ML tooling, LLM integrations, prompt engineering, evals, and MCP servers.
  • Experience mentoring other engineers. 

Bonus points

  • Experience with the Databricks platform (Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, Databricks Apps, Workflows).
  • Strong SQL proficiency.
  • Familiarity with identity and access management systems (Okta, Opal, Google Workspace).
  • Experience building mobile applications (iOS/Android).
  • Experience with SaaS management, procurement systems, or IT operations tooling.
  • Background in data governance, schema design, access control, and data quality monitoring.
  • Experience working with distributed teams across time zones.

 

Pay Range Transparency

Databricks is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles.  Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, relevant certifications and training, and specific work location. Based on the factors above, Databricks anticipates utilizing the full width of the range. The total compensation package for this position may also include eligibility for annual performance bonus, equity, and the benefits listed above. For more information regarding which range your location is in visit our page here.

$159,900—$219,900 USD

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Starburst

Starburst delivers enterprise intelligence at scale by giving organizations secure, governed access to all their data, wherever it lives. Built for distributed data environments, Starburst helps enterprises power AI and analytics without the cost and complexity of traditional data consolidation. With open standards including Trino and Apache Iceberg, Starburst enables trusted access to complete enterprise context while helping organizations avoid vendor lock-in. Leading global enterprises trust Starburst to fuel AI, analytics, and enterprise intelligence. Learn more at starburst.ai.

About the role

As a Senior Systems Software Engineer on the Build & Delivery team, you ll own the systems that every team at Starburst ships through — the backend services and infrastructure of one trusted, self-service, increasingly autonomous delivery platform. You will help design and build the core delivery infrastructure, as well as build “the machine that builds the machine” that is used to ship across Starburst Enterprise, Galaxy, and customer-managed deployments at scale. Daily tasks will include developing backend services and infrastructure, building operational tooling, supporting our platform in production, and driving the reliability, scalability, and cost-efficiency of how we deliver software.

The problems are concrete: keep the mainline green by construction, so a red build always means a real defect; provision production-like environments on demand instead of a shared staging bottleneck; deliver testing as a service across every repo; and treat AI as a first responder for test maintenance, failure triage, and remediation.

As a Senior Systems Software Engineer you will:

  • Design and build the core services and infrastructure of the delivery platform, following the immutable cloud infrastructure paradigm, consistent across Starburst Enterprise, Galaxy, and customer-managed deployments
  • Build the merge-orchestration and gating systems that keep the mainline green by construction, including flaky-test detection and auto-quarantine
  • Build Testing-as-a-Service — shared, on-demand test infrastructure, intelligent test selection, and unified coverage and quality gates for every team
  • Build the service that provisions production-like environments on demand, so every change is proven and dogfooded before customers see it
  • Design the AI workflows in the delivery loop — test maintenance, failure triage, and remediation — validated before rollout
  • Own the reliability, scalability, and cost-efficiency of the platform in production
  • Continuously improve our engineering processes, tests, and systems that allow us to scale the code base and productivity of the team
  • Provide considerate and timely review of your peers pull requests and design proposals

Some of the things we look for:

  • Passion for software engineering, with an interest in build, delivery, and infrastructure engineering in particular
  • Experience designing, building, and operating distributed backend systems in production
  • Experience building for reliability, scalability, and efficiency at scale
  • Experience developing software in Java and Typescript
  • Cloud infrastructure architecture and orchestration experience
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and related tooling such as Pulumi or Terraform
  • Interest in applying AI and agentic workflows to engineering problems, with a validate-then-deploy discipline
  • Prior experience building CI/CD, merge queues, test infrastructure, or ephemeral environments is a strong plus
  • Prior experience in developing for or operating Trino is a plus
  • Demonstration of ownership, grit, and bias for action - core values at Starburst
  • Ability to Travel: This role will require occasional in-person travel for purposes including but not limited to new hire onboarding, team and department offsites, customer engagements, and other company events. Actual travel expectations may vary by role and business needs.

Build your career at Starburst

All-Stars have the opportunity and freedom to realize their true potential. By building alongside top talent, we’re empowered to take ownership of our careers and drive meaningful change. Anchored in industry-proven technology and unprecedented success, All-Stars are taking on the challenge everyday to disrupt our industry –  and the future. 

Our global workforce is supported by a competitive Total Rewards program that reflects our commitment to a rewarding and supportive work environment. This includes a variety of benefits like competitive pay, attractive stock grants, flexible paid time off, and more. 

We are committed to fostering an intentional, inclusive, and diverse culture that drives deep engagement, authentic belonging, and an exceptional All-Star experience. We believe that diversity of thought, perspective, background and experience will enable us to own what we do, drive our success and empower our All-Stars to show up authentically.

 or local laws.

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. Okta s Identity Governance (OIG) organization is looking for a Staff Engineer to join our Identity Administration team — a team that is directly responsible for one of the most critical and visible workflows in enterprise identity: how employees request, approve, and gain access to the resources they need. 

Opportunity

As a Staff Engineer on the OIG Identity Administration team, you will be involved in development, design, and maintenance of our product to serve enterprise customers at scale. You will involve the development and evolution of our product features — spanning the across different identity entities and personas — and work collaboratively across engineering, product, and design to deliver features that are secure, scalable, and delightful to use.

This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, leads with craft, and is energized by the challenge of building enterprise-grade software that millions of users depend on.

This is a rare opportunity to join a team where your technical decisions will directly shape how thousands of enterprises manage access governance at scale, where the technical challenges are genuinely hard, and where the work you ship will be seen and felt by real users every day.

 

Job Duties And Responsibilities

 

  • Take end-to-end ownership of feature areas — from technical design through implementation, testing, deployment, and post-launch monitoring
  • Design, build, and ship high-quality, production-ready features across the OIG system, with a focus on correctness, reliability, and performance
  • Quickly deliver high-quality bug fixes and handle customer-reported issues
  • Write clean, well-tested, maintainable code and hold yourself and teammates to a high bar for engineering quality
  • Partner with our Product Development, QA, and Site Reliability Engineering teams for scoping the development and deployment work

 

Required knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • 8 to 13 years of experience with Java (Spring/Dropwizard) and/or Golang, with a deep understanding of multi-threading and asynchronous processing.
  • Understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and JWT tokens, specifically for service-to-service communication.
  • Demonstrated AI fluency in agentic systems and modern AI applications.
  • Experience building high-performance RESTful APIs and/or gRPC services with in-depth knowledge in distributed systems / micro services architectures.
  • Solid experience with relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL) and caching layers (Redis) at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS (Fargate, EC2, Lambda) and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform). You should be comfortable managing your own cloud resources.
  • Strong proficiency with containerization (Docker/Kubernetes) and CI/CD automation tools (Jenkins, ArgoCD, or GitHub Actions).

Nice to haves:

  • Experience with Splunk, SignalFX, or Datadog for monitoring and troubleshooting production issues.
  • Familiarity with Kafka or SQS for handling cross-org asynchronous events.
  • Basic familiarity with React/JavaScript to help integrate backend services.
  • Understanding of how to build and deploy services across isolated infrastructure units

 Education and Training:

  • B.S. Computer Science or related field

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn t a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you re ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase.

Join the Money Movement team within the Developer product group and help build the infrastructure powering the future of global payments. CDP brings together payments, trading, wallets, and stablecoins through a single onboarding flow and self-service APIs. You ll design and build backend systems for stablecoin-based pay-ins, payouts, deposits, and withdrawals, enabling fast, secure, and scalable transfers that underpin how value moves across the Coinbase ecosystem and beyond.

What you ll do:

  • Own key projects end-to-end as the Directly Responsible Individual, driving stablecoin-based money movement features from system design through production deployment with high accountability.
  • Build backend systems, infrastructure, and internal/external APIs that enable businesses and partners to embed stablecoin-powered payments into their products.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Infrastructure, and Compliance to translate requirements into robust, scalable solutions that balance speed, security, and regulatory needs.
  • Execute performance, scalability, and reliability improvements across distributed systems, identifying bottlenecks and driving fixes before they impact customers.
  • Support the team s engineering quality through code reviews, architectural best practices, and contributing to patterns that raise the technical bar.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 2+ years of software engineering experience building and operating backend systems, ideally in fintech, payments, or crypto.
  • Proficiency in backend languages (e.g., Go, Java) and cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, GCP), with hands-on experience designing distributed systems and APIs.
  • Track record of serving as DRI for technical projects, driving end-to-end delivery from system design through production deployment.
  • Experience integrating with or building on blockchain or crypto technologies such as stablecoins, on-chain payments, or smart contract platforms (e.g., Ethereum, Solana, Base).
  • Demonstrated ability to write technical design documents and communicate architecture trade-offs to product and engineering stakeholders.
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Job: P78197

Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)). 

 

Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus):
$152,405—$179,300 USD

  • Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

As a founding Staff Software Engineer on the AI Developer Productivity within the Institutional Product Group, you ll build and roll out agentic AI workflows that transform how Institutional engineers write, review, and ship code. This team is aligned with Coinbase s AI developer tooling vision but dedicated to the unique needs of Institutional s trading, custody, and financial infrastructure systems. You ll own the design and delivery of AI-powered capabilities that drive continuous code improvement, accelerate development cycles, and raise the quality bar across one of Coinbase s most critical product groups.

What you’ll do: 

  • Own the architecture and delivery of agentic AI workflows for continuous code improvement, including automated refactoring, test generation, and proactive bug detection tailored to Institutional systems
  • Build developer productivity tooling that integrates LLM-powered agents into the Institutional engineering workflow, from code review through deployment
  • Partner with Platform s AI and DevX teams to align on shared infrastructure while customizing capabilities for Institutional s unique reliability, security, and regulatory requirements
  • Drive adoption of AI-assisted development practices across Institutional engineering, measuring impact on velocity, code quality, and developer satisfaction
  • Shape technical standards and best practices for human-AI collaborative development within the Institutional org, ensuring safe and governed use of AI agents in high-stakes financial systems

Required skills and experience:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience with at least 2 years building AI/LLM-powered developer tools, agentic workflows, or code automation systems
  • Proven track record of designing and shipping production-grade systems that integrate LLMs or AI agents into software development lifecycles (e.g., code generation, automated review, CI/CD automation)
  • Deep fluency in Java, Python, Go, or similar backend languages, with hands-on experience building and orchestrating AI agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, or custom agent architectures)
  • Demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with platform, infrastructure, and product teams to deliver tooling adopted by hundreds of engineers
  • Familiarity with financial systems, high-reliability engineering, or regulated environments where correctness, auditability, and security are non-negotiable

jobs.title: [CONTRACT] Part-Time Sales Compensation Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCKER

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________



Location: Remote (100%) with preference for Mountain or Pacific time zone

Contract Duration: 3 months, with possible extension

Hours: 20-30 hours per week

_______________________________________________________________________




ABOUT THE ROLE

Docker is looking for a Sales Compensation Analyst to join our Finance team on a contract basis and support the administrative backbone of our sales compensation program. This is a writing-heavy, detail-oriented role. You'll draft and maintain participation agreements, create clear documentation, and manage SPIFF programs in our compensation system.

If you can turn complex comp plan language into clear, accurate, plain-English documents, and you enjoy the operational side of sales comp, this role is for you.

_______________________________________________________________________




WHAT YOU'LL DO


PARTICIPATION AGREEMENTS

 - Draft, edit, and finalize sales compensation participation agreements and plan documents

 - Make sure plan terms, quotas, payout mechanics, and eligibility language are accurate and consistent

 - Manage agreement distribution, tracking, and signature follow-up

 - Partner with Legal, HR, and Sales leadership to review and approve language


DOCUMENTATION

 - Write and maintain comp plan documentation, process guides, and policy FAQs

 - Create step-by-step procedures for recurring comp admin tasks

 - Keep documentation current as plans, territories, and policies change


SPIFF ADMINISTRATION

 - Set up, configure, and maintain SPIFF programs in the compensation system

 - Track eligibility, calculate payouts, and validate results against program rules

 - Answer SPIFF questions from sales reps and managers

 - Audit program data for accuracy before payouts are finalized


GENERAL SALES COMP SUPPORT

 - Help with commission data validation, reconciliation, and dispute resolution

 - Support quota, territory, and roster updates in the comp system

 - Respond to rep inquiries with clarity and professionalism



_______________________________________________________________________




WHAT YOU BRING


REQUIRED

 - 1-2 years of sales compensation experience

 - Strong written communication skills, with a proven ability to write clear, precise, professional documents

 - High attention to detail and comfort working with plan rules, rates, and payout logic

 - Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets

 - Ability to manage multiple deliverables and deadlines independently in a fully remote environment


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hands-on SPIFF administration experience

 - Experience working in a sales compensation system (for example Xactly, Varicent, CaptivateIQ, Performio, SAP Commissions, or similar)

 - Experience drafting or editing participation agreements or comp plan documents

 - Familiarity with CRM data (Salesforce) and how it feeds comp calculations

_______________________________________________________________________




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Participation agreements go out accurate, on time, and with minimal back-and-forth

 - Documentation is clear enough that reps and managers can find answers on their own

 - SPIFFs are set up correctly and paid without errors or disputes

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Control Planes
jobs.description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply.  Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.




THE MISSION:

At Kong, we are pioneering the Agentic Era of service connectivity by building the infrastructure that powers the modern API world. As a Software Engineer on the Konnect Control Plane team, you will architect the next-generation cloud-hosted control plane that manages global customer configurations seamlessly.

Your work will directly empower developers worldwide, ensuring high availability, speed, and seamless connectivity for Kong’s flagship service connectivity platform.



WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Architect and scale microservices that power Kong Konnect’s cloud-hosted control plane to manage global customer configurations seamlessly.

 - Design, implement, and maintain highly performant, low-latency APIs and services that deliver exceptional Developer Delight.

 - Drive solutions for technical problems of moderate complexity, keeping an active focus on preventing technical debt.

 - Prevent regressions and guarantee product stability by writing robust, automated tests.

 - Own the reliability and uptime of services in production by participating in an active on-call rotation.

 - Collaborate closely with Product Management, Solutions Architects, and cross-functional engineering teams to implement impactful business features.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING:



THE TOOLKIT

 - 5+ years of experience working in a team environment to develop, deliver, and maintain complex, distributed software solutions.

 - Solid proficiency in Go (Golang) and designing relational database data models.

 - Practical experience building, debugging, and maintaining microservices architectures at scale.

 - Demonstrated experience performing DevOps monitoring, observability, and supporting a large-scale SaaS platform running on Kubernetes and containerized environments.

 - Working knowledge of L4/L7 proxies such as Nginx, HA-proxy, or Envoy.

 - Firm grasp of API lifecycle management, design standards, and testing frameworks (TDD/automated testing).

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.


THE KONG DNA

 - Ownership: You act as a driver, not a passenger, and take complete accountability for the quality of your systems and outcomes.

 - Urgency: You thrive in a high-growth environment, iterating quickly and pushing for results with passion and grit.

 - Collaboration: You break down silos, communicate transparently, and model the true spirit of a team player.


BONUS POINTS:

 - Deep experience with Go standards and writing idiomatic, highly optimized Go.

 - Direct experience with Nginx, OpenResty, LuaJIT, or the Kong gateway core.

 - Experience with cloud-native observability stacks, specifically Datadog or OpenTelemetry.

 - Active contributions to open-source software projects.

#LI-AW1



About Kong: 

Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit www.konghq.com http://www.konghq.com.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Tech Lead, Travel
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Ramp Travel team builds the travel booking and management platform built-in to Ramp. We build the capabilities that allows travelers to stay productive on the road: flight and hotel search, booking and checkout, our agentic travel assistant, and on-the-go mobile trip guidance. We also own the capabilities that ensure companies are spending their travel dollars effectively: travel policy evaluation, supplier and TMC integrations and benchmarking, and data insights.

Growing the sophistication and global reach of the Travel product is a top strategic priority at Ramp. The work this team does directly enables Ramp to to support some of the largest and most interesting customers in the world.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead, mentor, coach, and grow the Ramp Travel engineering team (~6 engineers today).

 - Own delivery across our travel management surfaces: search and inventory, quoting and repricing, checkout, policy evaluation, loyalty, post-booking servicing.

 - Own reliability and correctness of a system dependent on third parties: supplier APIs, GDS and aggregator content, TMC and OBT integrations.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Ops, Partnerships, and Sales on enterprise travel commitments.

 - Set the team's practices for AI-assisted development and ship agentic booking features.

 - Hire. The team is expected to grow.


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 2+ years managing engineers, team size roughly 5 to 15.

 - High levels of ownership. Comfortability taking difficult ambiguous problems and driving successful execution.

 - Has built something 0→1 and then scaled it.

 - Willing to be hands-on. This is a six-person team, and everyone at Ramp is a builder.

 - Current enough technically to lead a design review and evaluate an architecture proposal.

 - Strong product judgment and comfort talking to customers.

 - Has owned a transactional system with external dependencies: booking, payments, marketplace, or logistics.


PREFERRED

 - Corporate travel domain experience, such as: corporate online booking tools (OBTs), integrations with travel content sources (GDS/NDC), and front-end traveler experiences.

 - Enterprise B2B fintech or T&E background.

 - Has rolled out agentic dev tooling to a team, or shipped LLM-backed features.




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
   
   


CANADA

 - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

 - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

 - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health




UNITED KINGDOM

 - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

 - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

 - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay




REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 


OTHER NOTICES

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com http://Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Analytics
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on  staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.



RESPONSIBILITIES

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

 - Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.

 - Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.

 - Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.

 - Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.

 - Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.

 - Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.

 - Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.

 - Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.


QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams

 - Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail

 - Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right

 - Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO

 - Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running

jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Director - Finance Solutions
jobs.description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




YOUR MISSION

Finance teams lose hours every week chasing approvals, re-keying data, and reconciling records across systems that don’t talk to each other. As a member of UiPath’s product marketing team, you’ll bring our agentic solutions for the Office of the CFO to market, focusing on the source-to-pay and order-to-cash functions. These solutions orchestrate work across the ERP, procurement, and receivables systems customers already run. Drawing on your knowledge of how finance organizations buy and what they’re measured on, you’ll own positioning, launches, and sales enablement that speak to finance leaders in their own terms.




WHAT YOU’LL DO AT UIPATH

 - Lead go-to-market strategy and launch planning for source-to-pay (invoice processing, procurement, and supplier communications) and order-to-cash (collections and cash application), working with the field marketing and sales teams that bring it to market.

 - Define positioning and messaging for the full CFO buying center, from AP, AR, and procurement leaders to controllers and the CFO, presenting UiPath as the layer that orchestrates work across their existing systems rather than replacing them.

 - Build the sales story and the tools to tell it: pitch decks, battlecards, ROI calculators, demo narratives, objection handling, and sales training.

 - Recruit customer advocates and turn their results into proof points tied to finance KPIs such as DSO, cost per invoice, and on-contract spend.

 - Run buyer research, including personas, buying journeys, and win/loss analysis, and share what you learn with product management to shape the roadmap.

 - Develop the messaging, content, and audience insight behind campaigns across demand generation, field, and partner channels, and support analyst relations.

 - 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 10+ years in B2B marketing, consulting, or product development, ideally including SaaS product marketing for finance, procurement, or order-to-cash software.

 - Deep knowledge of source-to-pay and order-to-cash processes and the finance leaders who own them. Experience in finance operations, shared services, or finance advisory is a strong plus.

 - Working knowledge of enterprise SaaS, GenAI, agentic AI, and automation, including how they integrate with ERP and other systems of record, and the ability to explain them in terms of business outcomes.

 - A track record of successful launches built on sharp positioning, messaging, and sales collateral.

 - Clear, persuasive communication with every audience, from AP specialists to the CFO, in writing, in meetings, and on stage.

 - Experience partnering closely with marketing, sales, partners, product management, and engineering.

 - Hands-on use of AI tools in your day-to-day work, such as research, content development, and analysis, is a plus.

 - A degree in business, finance, accounting, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.



Maybe you don’t tick all the boxes above—but still think you’d be great for the job? Go ahead, apply anyway. Please. Because we know that experience comes in all shapes and sizes—and passion can’t be learned.

Many of our roles allow for flexibility in when and where work gets done. Depending on the needs of the business and the role, the number of hybrid, office-based, and remote workers will vary from team to team. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis and there is no fixed deadline for this requisition. The application window may change depending on the volume of applications received or may close immediately if a qualified candidate is selected.

We value a range of diverse backgrounds, experiences and ideas. We pride ourselves on our diversity and inclusive workplace that provides equal opportunities to all persons regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and expression, national origin, disability, neurodiversity, military and/or veteran status, or any other protected classes. Additionally, UiPath provides reasonable accommodations for candidates on request and respects applicants' privacy rights. To review these and other legal disclosures, visit our privacy policy https://www.uipath.com/legal/trust-and-security/privacy-policy.

jobs.description: Staff Engineer You'll be the most senior engineer on the agents that run finance operations for our customers — designing, building, and operating the autonomous agents that handle accounts payable and receivable end-to-end. From invoice validation and dispute resolution to cross-company negotiation and cash optimization. This is an individual-contributor role at the top of our ladder: no direct reports, full technical authority over the architecture the rest of the team builds on. What you'll do Agent architecture — Design the multi-agent system: agent boundaries, event contracts, orchestration patterns, and the separation between LLM reasoning and deterministic enforcement. LLMs inform; rules enforce. You own where that line sits for every action that moves money, and the authorization gateway that makes it non-negotiable. Agentic dispute resolution — An agent that reads the claim, gathers the evidence from the PO, contract, and delivery record, forms a position, and works it to settlement — negotiating with the counterparty where that's appropriate, escalating to a human where it isn't. Deductions and short pays classified, tied to the underlying claim, and driven to resolution rather than parked in an aging bucket. Agentic dynamic discounting — Agents that continuously price early payment against the cash position on both sides of the transaction, propose terms, and execute them. Static payment terms become a negotiation that runs on its own. Matching and reconciliation — Three-way matching across purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice with configurable tolerances; cash application against bank statements and remittance advices, including partial payments and residuals; the exception paths that follow when any of it fails. Unglamorous but important: The foundation everything agentic sits on. Validation & anomaly detection — Business rule checks, duplicate and near-duplicate detection, pricing discrepancy detection, and anomaly detection across time. Precision matters as much as recall here: a false positive is a blocked supplier and an angry procurement lead. Integration framework — ERP systems first and deepest, then banking APIs, accounting platforms, Gmail, Drive, and Slack. Auth model, credential lifecycle, data normalization. Today each connector is a project; you make the next one a configuration. Compliance & security — Agents operate within a zero-trust model. You'll design how agents verify independently against source data, how outbound content is reviewed, and how the system prevents cascading failures from prompt injection. Plus the European e-invoicing mandates now landing across France, Germany, and Spain, and what EN 16931 means for the pipeline. Platform & data infrastructure — Own the primitives every agent action rests on: an append-only PostgreSQL event store with tamper-evident hash chaining for replay and audit; cryptographic signature verification on agent events and approval chains before anything external fires; the Workflow Constraint Engine that gates payments, emails, and API calls on deterministic policy, not model output; row-level multi-tenancy and tenant-scoped credentials across every data store; attribute-based authorization via Cerbos, evaluated the same way whether the caller is an agent or a human; and the MCP security layer — auth, capability-scoping, rate limiting — for external agent-to-agent access. The engineering standard — Architecture decision records, review bar, on-call, and a clear view of what we deliberately don't build. You'll write the things the next ten engineers read in week one, and you'll spend time with controllers and AP leads watching agents fail in ways no test predicted. What we're looking for 8+ years shipping production systems; currently Staff, Principal, Lead IC, or a founding engineer. You've carried an architecture through a scaling step and lived with your own decisions. Strong systems design thinking — agent boundaries, failure modes, trust boundaries, contract evolution. Money movement is not retry-safe by default and you already know why. Depth in Python and/or TypeScript in production, and deep PostgreSQL: event sourcing, row-level security, indexing tradeoffs, schema evolution under load. Hands-on experience with LLM-powered systems, agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or similar), and document AI (LlamaIndex, LlamaParse, or similar). Strong opinions about when to use an LLM vs. a rules engine vs. traditional ML — and the courage to defend them. Experience designing data pipelines, integration architectures, or event-driven systems in production. Security awareness — you think about what happens when untrusted input meets your pipeline, and about segregation of duties before someone makes you. Technical leadership without a title: reviews that teach, designs that get adopted, engineers who get faster because you're there. Effective use of AI coding tools with strong review skills for LLM integration and auth code. Domain knowledge across the purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash cycle. jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Platform
jobs.description: Orbital Industries is an AI Industrial company, with frontier AI embedded at every step in the production of critical physical products - from creating advanced materials to engineering and manufacturing. Every Orbital Industries product is developed using CurieOS, our AI operating system, uniting AI-automated hardware engineering with AI-designed material science to achieve breakthrough real-world performance. We also offer CurieOS to our customers and partners, extending the same platform and workflows that power Orbital Industries to their own teams and products. We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing. Working at Orbital Industries means working in vertically integrated teams across the full stack, from molecules to manufacturing. We're looking for people who have a love of physical technology, curiosity in AI and a desire to learn. The role Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced. The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do. This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is. How we work We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out. You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production. What you'll work on first In your first six months you'll work across the parts of CurieOS that customers have to be able to trust. Like everyone on the team you'll touch most of them, and go deepest where your interests take you: Tenancy, isolation and identity. How CurieOS keeps each customer separate, from shared multi-tenant accounts to dedicated single-tenant deployments. That covers data isolation, SSO and access control. You'll also be an engineering voice in customer security reviews. Release and production. How changes get to production safely: release gates, staged rollouts and rollback, automated smoke tests, on-call and incident response. We ship often, and you'll build what lets us keep doing that without breaking what customers rely on. Agent quality in production. Measuring how well agents perform on real customer workflows, working with our researchers to bring the latest evals into the platform, and using those measurements to decide what is good enough to release. A model or prompt change should have to pass the same gate as a code change. Observability and cost. Knowing the platform is healthy and what it costs. That means SLOs, tracing and alerting, plus cost telemetry and usage metering for every workflow and every customer, so we can see where model and compute spend goes and make deliberate choices about it. Infrastructure and deployment. One standard for how CurieOS is deployed, configured and upgraded in each environment, across our own cloud accounts, GPU capacity and customer-dedicated deployments. Where the platform is going Once those foundations are solid, there's a lot to shape next: Traceable results. Provenance for every number an agent produces: which inputs, tools, models and versions went into it, so our users can check it and sign it off. Agent runtime and context. How agents plan, call tools, manage context across long-running work and hand off to people at the right moment. Durable workflows. Orchestration that survives failures, retries and runs lasting hours, mixing agent steps with deterministic calculations. At Staff level, you'd set technical direction across these areas, not just within one. You'd own one of them end to end, run the design reviews that our research and forward deployed teams build on, make the architecture calls that are hard to reverse, and help shape how we hire and grow engineers. Our stack Python services on Kubernetes, running on AWS plus specialist GPU clouds for heavy compute. Strong engineers from Go, Kotlin, Java or a comparable stack will pick up the language quickly. What matters more is that you've run real systems in the cloud. You'll have most of these Designed and built backend services that other teams or customers relied on, and made the key decisions yourself. Owned a system in production after it shipped: the cloud infrastructure it ran on, on-call, incidents, how changes went out, and the monitoring that told you it was healthy. Built and run something where LLMs do real work for real users, and dealt with the cost, latency and quality trade-offs that come with it. Used coding agents heavily in your own work, with opinions on where they help and where they break. Led a project end to end, made trade-offs you can explain, and raised the bar for the engineers around you. The AI Governance and Control (AIGC) platform understands user / agent intent and data context in real time, giving security teams visibility and control across every tool and workflow so companies can move faster with AI while minimizing risk. We operate in one of the fastest-moving spaces in tech: the emerging intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It's a market still being defined, and we're among the first to build natively for it - protecting sensitive data in real time, at the endpoint, with minimal friction for the teams using it. Enterprises get full visibility and control. Their people get to innovate without guardrails slowing them down. Named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, Harmonic is gaining serious recognition and serious traction. We're led by deep cybersecurity expertise and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel. As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. That's what we build. How We Work: AI-First by Design Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work, from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity. For some, this involves tinkering and remaining open to emerging tools; for others, it means architecting entirely new systems with AI at the core.
