jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Code Forge
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Developer Productivity organization works to make Stripe the most productive place of an engineer’s career. The Code Review team builds the tools and processes that help Stripe engineers review and ship code safely and efficiently. We treat engineers’ attention as a valuable resource, building tools that help them understand changes and focus on the decisions that need human judgment.

Our goal is to build an AI review agent that outperforms human review at preventing problems after changes merge, while helping developers move quickly. We are also moving code review from GitHub to Orbit Diffs, Stripe’s own review interface, and enabling Stripe’s migration from legacy source control infrastructure to new systems, including infrastructure built at Stripe.

What you’ll do

As a Staff Software Engineer, you will take ownership of problems across the code review domain, set technical direction, and build alignment across Stripe. You will combine technical leadership with hands-on engineering to build the systems that determine which changes can be approved by agents and when human judgment is needed. Your decisions will influence both the pace and safety of changes across Stripe.

You will work across user interfaces, backend services, source control integrations, and agent harnesses. Our team works primarily in Go, Ruby, and TypeScript, and you will use the technologies each problem requires. As AI capabilities evolve, you will experiment with new approaches and turn them into reliable, maintainable tools for developers.

Responsibilities

  • Set technical direction for code review, build alignment across Stripe, and mentor engineers as you lead complex projects from problem definition through delivery and adoption
  • Build and improve agent harnesses that enable review agents to exercise judgment and safely approve pull requests
  • Develop evaluations that compare agent and human review decisions, assess the safety of merged changes and the impact on developer velocity, and guide improvements to approval decisions
  • Evaluate and apply advances in AI and agent orchestration to accelerate engineering delivery across Stripe while maintaining review quality, maintainability, reliability, and change safety
  • Build and maintain Orbit Diffs and the surrounding code review tools, helping engineers understand changes and focus their attention where their judgment is most valuable
  • Improve code ownership, intelligent reviewer assignment, stacked pull request workflows, and controls for change management
  • Support Stripe’s migration to new source control infrastructure by adapting code review workflows and integrations
  • Partner with security, compliance, infrastructure, reliability, and language and runtime teams to improve how software changes are evaluated and approved across Stripe

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • BS or MS in Computer Science or a related field
  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, including designing, building, and operating reliable production software across languages and system boundaries
  • Experience owning a technical domain, setting technical direction, and leading complex projects from ambiguous problems through delivery
  • Experience using data and user feedback to evaluate quality, understand user needs, and guide engineering decisions
  • Experience building alignment across teams, explaining technical tradeoffs, and adapting your approach as technologies evolve

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building agent harnesses, orchestrating agents, or designing evaluations for agent behavior
  • Experience building developer productivity tools, especially code review or related workflows
  • Experience with software change management and compliance, including designing, implementing, or maintaining controls

jobs.description:

About the Engineering team 

The Engineering team builds systems that power Affirm’s mission. We take pride in our craft, building reliable, performant, and scalable solutions that touch every part of the business. Whether we’re enabling new ways to pay, ensuring our platforms can scale to the most demanding levels in the industry, or developing seamless servicing experiences, our focus is on solving complex problems through exceptional engineering.

About the team

ML Feature Platform is one of the two teams that compose the ML Platform at Affirm, the other team being ML Training & Serving Platform. The two platform teams work closely together to create the ML + Data flywheel that empowers Affirm. 

ML Feature Platform’s mission is to: Grow Affirm’s business by building a delightful, self-serve platform for developing and serving data for machine learning and decisioning.

As the feature platform team, we own multiple artifacts that in aggregate own the end-to-end flows for features. This includes: 

  • Feature creation, exploration, and serving
  • Data storage, availability, and visibility
  • Offline backfilling infrastructure and platform improvements

This scope means your work will have a direct impact on the everyday lives and capabilities for our end users: MLEs, Analysts, and decisioning teams. Additionally as the primary data source for ML and online decisioning, our platform’s performance is critical to Affirm’s availability and latency goals.

We’re looking for engineers who are passionate about ML enablement and believe that platform level improvements can bring snowball effects across the company.

 

What you’ll do

  • You will be responsible for owning and delivering quarterly goals for your team, leading engineers on your team through ambiguity to solve open-ended problems, and ensuring that everyone is supported throughout delivery.
  • You will support your peers and stakeholders in the product development lifecycle by collaborating with product management, design & analytics by participating in ideation, articulating technical constraints, and partnering on decisions that properly consider risks and trade-offs.
  • You will proactively identify project, process, technology or business issues, advocate for them, and lead in solving them.
  • You will support the operations and availability of your team’s artifacts by creating and monitoring metrics, escalating when needed, and supporting “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
  • You will foster a culture of quality and ownership on your team by setting or improving code review and design standards for your team, and advocating for them beyond your team through your writing and tech talks.
  • You will help develop talent on your team by providing feedback and guidance, and leading by example.

What we look for

 

  • You have 4+ years of experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.
  • You have a track record of developing highly available distributed systems using technologies like AWS, MySQL and Kubernetes.
  • You have experience defining a technical plan for the delivery of a significant feature or system component with an elegant, simple and extensible design. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
  • You are proficient at making significant changes in a large code base, and have developed a suite of tools and practices that enable you and your team to do so safely.
  • · Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic s products are growing fast in reach and complexity. Every new model, product, and channel brings problems no one predicted. We want to catch each issue as early as possible, get customers unblocked fast, and fix the root cause. The best experience is one where a customer never has to ask for help.

We are building a Support Technology engineering team to solve what stands between a customer and Claude, whether they want to use it but can t or are unhappy with their experience. That covers individual users, businesses, and customers who reach Claude through partners.

Our goal is a better product experience for everyone who uses Claude. We make it easy for customers to get help and talk to us, through Claude itself and via human specialists with the tools to solve their problems. We also determine why they needed help and fix the cause in the product.

Billing is a good example. When a charge is confusing, a payment fails, or a plan doesn t unlock, a customer should be able to reach us and get it resolved in one conversation. Then we want to learn why it happened and change the product, whether that s the subscription flow, the payment error, or the invoice, so the next customer never has to ask.

As one of the team s early engineers, you will set the technical direction and build the core systems behind this work. We expect Claude to handle more of each case over time, from diagnosing an issue to resolving it to flagging the product fix behind it. Success means customers run into fewer problems, get them truly solved when they do, and are happy with the help they receive, whether it comes from Claude or a person.

This is a hands-on role with high leverage. You will write a lot of code and lead across teams, since many fixes belong to other product teams. You will partner with our Product Manager, the Product Support team, and product engineering teams such as Billing Platform.

Key responsibilities

  • Improve the product experience at the root: Build agents that spot where customers keep getting stuck and find the root cause, then ship the fix or drive it with the owning team until customers stop running into the problem
  • Make our support agents reliable first responders: Build the tools, APIs, and safe, audited workflows our Claude-powered support agents use for common fixes, with evals, guardrails, and clean handoffs to people, and measure whether customers problems actually get solved
  • Build the platform foundations: Create a reliable support platform that scales with our growth, including the experience and tools for customers and specialists, and the data that shows what customers are running into and whether our changes help
  • Support enterprise and partner channels: Extend support to business customers, admins, and partner-sold customers, including cases that start outside our own products
  • Raise the bar and build with Claude: Set standards for reliability, observability, testing, and rollouts, mentor engineers, and use Claude heavily in your own work

Minimum qualifications

  • Deep backend and distributed systems skills, including APIs, data models, event-driven systems, and third-party integrations
  • Experience building production software, including technical lead roles on multi-team projects
  • Experience building systems where correctness, access control, and auditability matter
  • A clear vision for how capable models like Claude can improve customer support, and motivation to build it
  • Judgment about when to ship a simple fix and when to invest in a platform
  • Track record of leading without formal authority and getting other teams to own and ship fixes

Preferred qualifications

  • 8+ years building backend or platform systems in production, including 3+ years leading large-scale, complex projects or teams as an engineer or tech lead
  • Experience building and improving customer-facing products with measurable impact
  • Experience with billing, payments, or subscription systems
  • Experience shipping LLM-based or agentic systems in production
  • Experience building with helpdesk or contact center platforms such as Intercom, Zendesk, or Salesforce Service Cloud
  • Experience building internal tools or platforms for operations teams such as support, risk, finance, or trust and safety
  • Experience building data pipelines for support or operations analytics
  • Full-stack experience, including web UIs for internal tools or customer-facing flows
  • Experience with enterprise features such as SSO, admin controls, or provisioning, or with partner and cloud marketplace integrations
  • Experience setting multi-year technical direction for an area and growing other senior engineers

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Platform Infrastructure - Dublin
jobs.description:
Astronomer empowers data teams to bring mission-critical software, analytics, and AI to life and is the company behind Astro, the industry-leading unified DataOps platform powered by Apache Airflow®. Astro accelerates building reliable data products that unlock insights, unleash AI value, and power data-driven applications. Trusted by more than 900 of the world’s leading enterprises, including Datadog, American Express, Expedia, Adobe, Autodesk, Together AI, and more, Astronomer lets businesses do more with their data. To learn more, visit www.astronomer.io http://www.astronomer.io.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

Astronomer’s products run on a complex, multi-cloud platform — and the scalability, and operational maturity of that platform is what we’re actively investing in. The work ahead on our Platform team isn’t about managing data or curating pipelines; it’s about building the foundational systems that everything else runs on — the kind of systems where the failure modes matter, the latency budgets are real, and getting it wrong has visible consequences for hundreds of enterprise customers.

We’re looking for a Staff-level engineer who has built production platform systems at scale before — not just consumed them. You’ve designed systems under load, reasoned carefully about failure, and made your colleagues’ lives better by giving them something solid and well-understood to build on top of. You write strategy documents and then write the code that proves them out. You’ve driven a decision through, and lived with the consequences.

This is a foundational role at a consequential moment: your work will directly shape what Astronomer’s products — Astro, Observe, and our IDE — are capable of over the next several years.


WHAT YOU GET TO DO

Astronomer has a healthy and complex infrastructure estate spanning multiple cloud providers, a mix of managed and self-hosted systems, and an increasingly ambitious set of requirements as our products evolve. We have a clear sense of where we need to go; we need the right person to figure out how to get there and then go build it.

This is a deeply technical role with a high bar for code, so you’re an experienced developer, ideally in Go. A substantial part of your impact also comes from setting direction: design docs, proposals, and bringing along teams you don’t manage. Prefer heads-down coding most of the week? This role may not be the best fit.

 - Blaze a Trail: Own and develop our platform infrastructure strategy, with the sponsorship and responsibility to match. Map out what we need, build the case, bring the affected teams along, and own the outcomes.

 - Be an Owner: Be directly involved in deciding what we work on and how we work on it. Make promises, and keep them.

 - Do Sensible Things: Make principled build vs. buy assessments and advocate for the right tools for the right job — not the fashionable ones, not the ones already in the estate just because they’re there.

 - Garage Door Open: Create and maintain comprehensive internal documentation and decision records for systems and processes. Participate in architectural forums and make principled, open decisions that the rest of the organization can learn from and hold us to.


IS THIS ROLE FOR YOU?

 - A small, senior team. No direct reports; you lead through influence, not management.

 - Broad scope. Our control plane, CI/CD, builds and releases, observability, secrets and networking, with internal teams as your customers.

 - Buy-in, not authority. You’ll often need agreement from teams you don’t manage.


WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE

 - Distributed systems depth, grounded in practice. You have a solid working model of how production systems fail — consistency and availability tradeoffs, failure cascades, backpressure, graceful degradation. You can draw the diagram, explain the failure modes at each node, and make a reasoned argument for which ones actually matter in a given context. NALSD https://sre.google/workbook/non-abstract-design/ thinking is how you naturally approach a new system design.

 - Kubernetes at operator depth. You know what happens inside the scheduler and the control loop when things go wrong, because you’ve been there. You’ve operated clusters under real load, not just deployed workloads onto them.

 - Strong Go proficiency. The platform team writes production Go. You should be fluent: you’ve built and shipped systems in it, and you have opinions about what good Go looks like.

 - Multi-cloud experience, not just multi-cloud exposure. You’ve made considered architectural decisions across AWS, GCP, and/or Azure — not just consumed managed services, but evaluated tradeoffs between them and lived with those decisions in production.

 - A track record of influence without authority. You’ve taken a proposal to teams you don’t manage, handled real pushback, changed minds with evidence, and known when and how to escalate. You can tell us specific stories about it.

 - Generalist platform breadth. You’ve worked hands-on across several of: Kubernetes, CI/CD, builds and releases, observability, networking and secrets management, rather than going deep in just one.

 - Strong written and verbal communication. You can write a design doc that changes minds, and a postmortem that makes the organization smarter. You’ve worked effectively in a globally-distributed team.


BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience with storage primitives at the system level — you’ve reasoned about when to reach for a relational store vs. an object store vs. something else, and you have real opinions informed by real failures.

 - Experience working on a SaaS/PaaS product across multiple cloud providers.

 - Familiarity with Apache Airflow or workflow orchestration systems.

A note on level: titles vary a lot between companies, and we level on scope of influence, not title.

jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Staff Software Engineer, Storage

Location: Bellevue, WA

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

We're at the forefront of the data revolution, committed to building the world's greatest data and applications platform. Our 'get it done' culture allows everyone at Snowflake to have an equal opportunity to innovate on new ideas, create work with a lasting impact, and excel in a culture of collaboration.

About the Team:

Snowflake's mission is to mobilize the world's data by building the greatest data and applications platform. Not just of the cloud era, but in the history of computing. To support this mission, the Storage team focuses on building the world's best storage platform. That means enhancing value-added services such as disaster recovery and AI integrations, and providing enterprise-grade, cloud-native storage for containerized workloads, especially in the fast-growing AI space.

We are seeking an outstanding Staff Software Engineer with a passion for large scale databases and distributed systems to help drive our continued growth. In this role, you'll connect customer needs with the business and technology, and act as a technical leader who helps the team carry out its vision.

We are at an inflection point as we continue to scale the footprint and expand the TAM of Snowflake through new and Neo Clouds onboarding, changes in the workloads, and need to simplify in order to enable Snowflake customers to unlock their full data potential.

AS A STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:

 - Translate business and customer needs into technical designs that deliver new capabilities to existing and new Snowflake customers

 - Drive innovation in how table data is stored, accessed, and processed in the Snowflake cloud

 - Architect, design, and implement new systems and solutions that advance the Snowflake Data Infrastructure platform

 - Collaborate closely with product managers, architects, other engineering teams, and cross-functional partners to design and build new technologies that go directly into our customers' hands

 - Provide technical leadership for your team, setting direction on design, code quality, and operational excellence

 - Mentor and coach engineers on your team and across partner teams

AN IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE MOST OF THE FOLLOWING QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 10+ years of industry experience designing, building, and supporting large-scale, durable distributed systems in production

 - An excellent team player who is committed to helping everyone around them reach their potential and grow

 - Alignment with the Snowflake values

 - A proven track record of leading and delivering large, complex projects across multiple teams in the storage space (object storage, data warehouses, SQL/NoSQL databases, distributed file systems, etc.)

 - Strong development skills and AI-forward mindset with a critical eye towards code maintainability

 - Experience with public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP)

 - Demonstrated ability to build alignment across teams and disciplines to bring complex technical solutions to life

If you're a leader who thrives in a fast-paced and dynamic environment and has a passion for shaping the future of storage technology, we'd love to hear from you!




Every Snowflake employee is expected to follow the company’s confidentiality and security standards for handling sensitive data. Snowflake employees must abide by the company’s data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee's duty to keep customer information secure and confidential.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
ABOUT HEX

Hex is growing our team of builders on a mission to make everyone a data person. Our platform solves key pain points with today’s data and analytics tooling, and empowers anyone to explore data using natural language, with or without code, on trusted context. Thousands of customers like Ramp https://hex.tech/customers/ramp/, Figma https://hex.tech/customers/figma/, Stubhub https://hex.tech/customers/stubhub/, Anthropic, and Gamma love Hex https://www.g2.com/products/hex-tech-hex/reviews for our beautiful UI, agentic superpowers, and boundless flexibility.

Hex has raised over $100M from leading investors like Sequoia, a16z, Snowflake and Amplify. With office hubs in San Francisco and New York, as well as remote team members throughout the US and UK, we’re a high-agency team that ships fast and has fun doing it. Check out our Intro to Hex video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qAXsnrNlavk and employee handbook https://www.notion.so/hexhq/Hex-Handbook-9fff0d42860e4f70815c599e0d1664d6 to learn more about what it’s like to work at Hex.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Hex's infrastructure team owns all of our cloud infrastructure (compute, networking, datastores) along with CI/CD and observability, across a multi-tenant platform and single-tenant environments. Every engineer at Hex depends on what the infrastructure team builds.

We're growing in customers, in users, and in the kinds of data workflows our workload compute backend has to support. That growth has opened up a set of projects that would meaningfully change how fast the rest of engineering ships, and we're hiring to take them on.

We're looking for someone who will pick up one of those projects, own it start to finish, and leave it better than they found it. Bring your opinions, including the ones that disagree with ours. Infrastructure tooling is changing quickly right now, and we want someone who's paying attention to that as we improve the foundational components that power Hex.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

Your first few months, we'll pick two or three of these together based on where you're strongest and where we're looking to invest:

 - CI/CD. Hex’s CI/CD pipelines need a glow-up: optimizing for speed, cost, and providing more flexibility.

 - Stack lifecycle. Setup, teardown, partial teardown, and updates for single-tenant stacks, today too much of this is manual and runs through our team.

 - Postgres at scale. Performance, migrations, and capacity for our multi-tenant production database.

 - Cost. Infrastructure spend visibility and reduction.

 - Security posture. Workload and container isolation, plus compliance work as we move upmarket.

 - Platform features. Customer-facing infrastructure capabilities: private connectivity, customer defined networking, and making single-tenant deployments easier to operate.


ABOUT YOU

 - 5+ years building and operating production infrastructure, including on-call

 - You make the people around you better, whether or not you've had the title

 - Strong Kubernetes operations: you can reason about scheduling, networking, and failure modes, not just apply manifests

 - Solid AWS fundamentals (EKS, RDS, VPC networking, IAM)

 - Infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform

 - Comfortable writing and reading enough application code to change a pipeline, a controller, or a service

 - You can take a vague, long-standing problem and turn it into something shippable without waiting to be told how

 - You write clearly, design docs and runbooks that engineers outside infra can follow

Plus depth in at least one of

 - Networking — VPC design, private connectivity (PrivateLink, peering), DNS, TLS and certificate management, agentic sandboxing

 - Databases — Postgres at scale: replication, tuning, connection pooling, major version upgrades, migrations under load

 - Deployment systems — CI/CD platform ownership, build performance and cost, release and artifact management




OUR STACK

 - Cloud: AWS (EKS, RDS, ElastiCache)

 - Databases: PostgreSQL (RDS), Redis, LanceDB, DynamoDB, MSK

 - Languages: TypeScript (Node.js), Python, Rust, Go

 - Infrastructure-as-code: Terraform

 - Monitoring: Datadog

The salary range for this role is: $246,000 - $329,000



In addition to our unique culture, Hex proudly offers a competitive total rewards package, including but not limited to, market-benched salary & equity, comprehensive health benefits, and flexible paid time off.

The salary range shown may be a reflection of additional factors such as geographical location and skill ranges/levels we’re open to. Placement in the salary range will be decided upon completion of the interview process, taking into account factors like leaving room for growth, internal fairness & parity, your demonstrated skills, and the depth of your experience. Our Recruiting team will be able to provide more details during the interview process.



By submitting an application the candidate consents to the use of their personal information in accordance with the Hex Privacy policy: https://learn.hex.tech/docs/trust/privacy-policy.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Sandbox
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCKER

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________




THE ROLE

The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead components of Docker Sandbox. You will own and drive this strategic product area from high-level concept design through delivery, adoption, and operation. You will help shape how developers and AI agents use fast, secure, isolated environments across local and cloud workflows. You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will help foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.



To thrive in this role, you will need experience working with developers, deep technical fluency in systems and developer infrastructure, and prior experience as a software engineer. You will need to understand containers, sandboxes/microVMs, virtualization technologies, hypervisors, the software development lifecycle, and how untrusted or agent-generated code can be safely executed and orchestrated. You will need a relentless drive to try new things and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap, earn the trust of the developer community, and scale reliable services. Most importantly, you will need to be comfortable taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

_______________________________________________________________________




RESPONSIBILITIES

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Self-Hosted and Connected Temporal
jobs.description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Temporal is used by a lot of companies in a wide variety of contexts. Many use Temporal Cloud. Many others users don’t yet know about Temporal Cloud, believe self-hosting is cheaper, and/or just don’t yet see a need to move. Still others (often happily using Temporal Cloud at large scale) also operate environments where a managed service isn't an option today and may never be, like:

 - AI and application companies embedding Temporal inside software their own customers run in isolated, air-gapped environments, or offering a remote management BYOA posture

 - Large enterprises keeping operational control of critical systems in-house by policy

 - Companies operating in sovereign clouds and similar contexts where legal or organizational requirements make outside management difficult or impossible

This role owns understanding the world of Temporal usage outside Cloud, what the different contexts demand, and where Temporal should (and shouldn't) engage. That includes what we build, what we support, what we charge for, and what we leave alone. You'll shape which offerings we pursue and how they make money or contribute to the larger business. Then you'll take the ones we commit to through launch and adoption.

Open source Temporal is central to this. We’re investing heavily in OSS, from performance improvements to easier management to clearer guidance on compatibility and cost. When companies write their apps on Temporal, they’re making a huge bet on us, and that trust is sacred. A large part of this role is improving and shepherding how we keep making OSS better.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Map usage outside Temporal Cloud. Build the company's clearest picture of where Temporal runs outside Cloud and why. Separate structural constraints (air gaps, regulation, owning operational risk) from cost, inertia, and/or other factors. Turn that into segments and use cases leadership can make decisions with.

 - Decide what we pursue. Recommend which needs deserve new offerings, which Temporal Cloud should cover, and which we deliberately leave alone. Write the case, defend it, and revisit it when the evidence changes.

 - Define the line between open source and paid. Set clear guidelines for which improvements and support go into open source Temporal, and where paid offerings take over. Keep the open source experience strong, and make the line easy for users and internal teams to understand.

 - Define the business model. Work with leadership, Sales, and Finance on packaging, pricing, and how we sell offerings that run outside our infrastructure. Know what customers will pay for and what it costs us to support it.

 - Help Cloud win where it should. Work with other PMs so workloads that can run on Cloud move there more easily, with a clear value and TCO case.

 - Lead without authority. Align Engineering, Resident Architects, Dev Success, Security, and go-to-market teams, including when their incentives conflict.

 - Own outcomes. Define success in terms of adoption, revenue, and retention. Use the results to steer further investment.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - A track record of setting product strategy, not only executing it. You've spotted a new offering or market, made the case for it, and seen it through to revenue.

 - Experience with infrastructure or platform products that customers operate themselves: open source, on-prem, or hybrid.

 - Commercial judgment. You can connect a customer problem to willingness to pay, pricing, and the cost of delivering and supporting the product.

 - Technical depth in distributed systems and operations: Kubernetes, databases, replication, upgrades, and failure recovery. You can go deep with engineers and turn the tradeoffs into product decisions.

 - Comfort saying "not this" and backing it with evidence. You change course when the facts change.

 - Clear writing. You can turn messy evidence from customers and the field into a recommendation leaders can act on.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience making money from open source or open-core products

 - Familiarity with air-gapped, regulated (FedRAMP, sovereign cloud), or bring-your-own-cloud environments

 - Experience selling to platform teams at large enterprises or AI companies

jobs.title: Product Manager | Bill Pay
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

Every business pays bills, and many of them still do it by hand. Someone opens the invoice, types it in, codes it, chases approvals, pays it, matches it and syncs it to the books. It's one of the largest manual workflows left in finance.

We're building the version where software does that work. Bills come in and get read, coded, matched, approved and paid, and a person steps in only when judgment matters. Bill Pay is already one of Ramp's fastest-growing products. The next few years decide who owns AP for the next decade, and we plan for it to be us.

We're looking for a PM who wants to build that.

 - Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week.

 - Level will be determined based on the candidate’s interview performance and previous scope of responsibility.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own strategy, roadmap and results for a major part of Bill Pay.

 - Spend real time with AP clerks, controllers and CFOs, and turn what you see into product.

 - Prototype with customers, set quality bars with Engineering and Data, and ship automation people trust.

 - Measure success by adoption, automation and time saved, then use the data to decide what comes next.

 - Work with Procurement, Accounting, Payments and Risk so a bill moves from inbox to payment to the books without gaps.


PROBLEMS YOU'LL WORK ON

 - How do we get from "AI drafts the bill" to "AI handles the bill" without customers losing trust or control?

 - When should an agent act on its own, when should it ask, and how do we show our work so a controller signs off with confidence?

 - How do we make one product that a 10-person startup sets up in minutes and a multi-entity enterprise with an ERP and an AP team runs at scale?

 - How do we catch the wrong bill, the duplicate and the suspicious vendor change before the money leaves?

 - How do we use what Ramp knows across millions of transactions to help customers pay smarter, not just faster?


WHAT YOU NEED

 - You have 5+ years building products, and you've owned at least one from first customer conversation to real adoption.

 - You've built with AI hands-on, whether in products, prototypes or side projects, and you have opinions about evals, failure modes and user control.

 - You're technical enough to go deep with engineers on data models and integrations, and you pull your own data.

 - You can make complex workflows simple without stripping out what power users need.

 - You learn new domains fast. You don't need to know AP today, but you'll want to know it better than anyone in six months.

 - You write clearly, decide quickly and get teams to ship.

 - You want a hard problem, a high bar and more scope as soon as you've earned it.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - You've worked on AP, payments, accounting or other finance software.

 - You've shipped AI to production, especially document understanding or agent workflows.

 - You've built for enterprise customers: ERPs, multi-entity setups, complex approvals and permissions.

 - You've worked at a high-growth startup and know what it takes to scale a product that's working.




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
   
   


CANADA

 - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

 - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

 - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health




UNITED KINGDOM

 - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

 - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

 - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay




REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 


OTHER NOTICES

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Databases
jobs.description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Staff Engineer on the Core Infra team at Harvey, you will define how our database infrastructure operates and evolves across our legal AI platform. Harvey runs a global fleet of PostgreSQL databases spanning multiple regions and availability zones. You’ll own the technical strategy for this fleet—setting the standards for migration governance, driving architecture decisions for multi-region scaling, and establishing the operational practices that keep our data layer reliable as we grow.

This is a leadership role with deep hands-on expectations. You’ll partner directly with Principal and Staff Engineers on infrastructure roadmap decisions while also being the person who can diagnose a replication lag spike at 2am. You’ll build the migration review framework, define the tooling strategy, and raise the bar for how the entire engineering organization thinks about database safety and performance.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use an in-person work model and offer relocation assistance to new employees.







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Migration Governance – Own the migration governance framework end-to-end—design the review workflow, CI gate checks, automated rollback procedures, and fleet-wide deployment sequencing that makes safe migrations the default across the org

 - Architecture & Scaling – Drive the technical strategy for Harvey’s global database fleet—multi-region replication design, capacity planning, sharding and partitioning approaches, and fleet-wide observability as we scale into new markets

 - Reliability & Performance – Own database reliability and performance at the fleet level—monitoring replication health, optimizing query performance, tuning vacuum and connection management, and building the alerting that gives us confidence across all production environments

 - Platform & Tooling – Build self-service tooling and developer guardrails—migration dry-runs, schema diff previews, automated health checks, performance regression detection—so engineering teams can move fast without bottlenecking on a single DBA

 - Incident Leadership – Lead database incident response and drive systemic improvements—triage production issues, run post-incident reviews, and turn lessons learned into durable process and tooling fixes

Even Better If You Can:

 - Security & Compliance – Partner with Security and Compliance to design and enforce data-layer controls for SOC 2, GDPR, and data residency requirements—access controls, audit logging, encryption standards, and data lifecycle policies

 - Strategic Partnership – Represent database engineering in vendor evaluations, build-vs-buy decisions, and technology strategy discussions with engineering leadership

 - Team Building – Shape the database engineering function at Harvey—define the operating model, set the hiring bar, mentor engineers on database best practices, and build the culture where teams proactively think about data safety
   
   





WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years of hands-on experience in database administration, database reliability engineering, or infrastructure engineering with PostgreSQL as your primary database, with demonstrated staff-level scope—you’ve set standards across teams, not just operated within one

 - Expert-level PostgreSQL knowledge (required)—WAL mechanics, vacuum tuning, logical and physical replication, partitioning strategies, and the ability to debug production issues others can’t. PostgreSQL is our core database and deep fluency is non-negotiable

 - Track record of building migration governance systems—not just reviewing migrations, but designing the frameworks, tooling, and organizational processes that make safe migrations the default

 - Experience architecting database infrastructure for multi-region, high-availability environments—replication topologies, failover automation, and data consistency trade-offs at fleet scale

 - Deep fluency with database observability—you’ve built monitoring strategies using Datadog, pganalyze, or custom instrumentation, and you know which metrics actually predict incidents

 - Experience leading database major version upgrades (e.g., PostgreSQL 14 → 16) or sharding initiatives in production with zero downtime

 - Proven ability to influence technical direction across teams without direct authority—you’ve written RFCs, set standards, and changed how an engineering organization thinks about database operations

 - Proficiency with cloud database services at scale (Azure Database for PostgreSQL, GCP Cloud SQL, or AWS RDS/Aurora) and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi)

 - Clear communication across audiences—you can present a database architecture decision to the VP of Engineering and explain a migration risk to a junior developer with equal clarit

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive - Oil & Gas
jobs.description:
LIFE AT UIPATH

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.

Could that be you?




YOUR MISSION

The Enterprise Accounts team at UiPath serves the largest companies in America, segmented by industry. In this role, you’ll own and grow a portfolio of existing Oil & Gas customers across upstream, midstream, downstream, and oilfield services. Your job is to expand UiPath’s footprint inside these accounts, taking automation from early wins in a single function to an enterprise-wide agentic automation program. You’ll work with the C-suite, Digital Transformation, IT, Finance, and Operations leaders to show how UiPath helps them run leaner, safer, and more efficiently in a volatile commodity market. You’ll be challenged and supported by the best in the industry as you build your own path to success.




WHAT YOU'LL DO AT UIPATH

 - Own a named set of Oil & Gas enterprise customers. Build account plans that map white space across business units, functions, and geographies to maximize expansion revenue.

 - Hit or beat quarterly and annual targets for expansion, upsell, cross-sell, and renewals.

 - Grow existing deployments into new use cases, such as joint interest billing, AFE and field ticket processing, land and lease administration, hydrocarbon and revenue accounting, procure-to-pay, maintenance work orders, HSE and regulatory reporting, and supply chain and logistics.

 - Position the full UiPath platform (agentic automation, document understanding, process and task mining, test automation) to move customers from tactical bots to strategic, scaled programs.

 - Build ROI and value cases that speak to O&G priorities: lower lifting and operating costs, capital discipline, margin protection during price swings, workforce productivity, and compliance.

 - Build executive relationships beyond the original buying center. Create champions in Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Land, HSE, and IT.

 - Work closely with Customer Success Managers to drive adoption, measure realized value, and turn success stories into new expansion opportunities.

 - Work with global systems integrators and energy-focused partners to find new opportunities and deliver successful implementations.

 - Track industry trends, competitors, M&A, and technology shifts in energy (ERP modernization, SAP S/4HANA migrations, energy transition initiatives) to anticipate customer needs.

 - Share wins, plays, and best practices with sales, solutions engineering, marketing, and industry teams.

 - Look for ways to use automation in your own daily work.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 7+ years of solution or value selling experience

 - 3+ years managing Enterprise Accounts, ideally in the Energy / Oil & Gas sector

 - A track record of growing revenue inside existing enterprise accounts through expansion, upsell, cross-sell, and multi-year renewals

 - Consistent quota attainment year over year

 - Working knowledge of Oil & Gas operations and back-office processes, and the ability to speak credibly with operations and finance leaders

 - Familiarity with the energy technology landscape (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Quorum, P2/Enertia, SCADA and field data systems) is a strong plus

 - Skill at explaining new, complex ideas simply, in a way that builds real demand for the solution

 - Ability to navigate large, matrixed, often geographically spread organizations and build relationships at many levels, up to the C-suite

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration and influence, both internally and externally

 - A research- and data-driven approach to account planning, and the habit of spotting opportunities in business-led conversations

 - A self-starter who is invested in the team’s success

 - Bachelor’s degree highly preferred

 - An automation-first mindset

 - Ability to travel 

 - Preference in location is Houston, but open to other areas in Texas







#LI-KS6

Maybe you don’t tick all the boxes above—but still think you’d be great for the job? Go ahead, apply anyway. Please. Because we know that experience comes in all shapes and sizes—and passion can’t be learned.

Many of our roles allow for flexibility in when and where work gets done. Depending on the needs of the business and the role, the number of hybrid, office-based, and remote workers will vary from team to team. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis and there is no fixed deadline for this requisition. The application window may change depending on the volume of applications received or may close immediately if a qualified candidate is selected.

We value a range of diverse backgrounds, experiences and ideas. We pride ourselves on our diversity and inclusive workplace that provides equal opportunities to all persons regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and expression, national origin, disability, neurodiversity, military and/or veteran status, or any other protected classes. Additionally, UiPath provides reasonable accommodations for candidates on request and respects applicants' privacy rights. To review these and other legal disclosures, visit our privacy policy https://www.uipath.com/legal/trust-and-security/privacy-policy.
